quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whatever position is safest for current road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever position is safest for current road conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on what is happening on the road.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: While turning.
Before turning.
By changing power suddenly in a turn.
By using the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before turning.
questions.explanation: You should shift gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. If someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks will likely be in their system 3 hours after the last drink?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find the minimum drinks remaining, subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. Someone who drank 7 drinks in 3 hours would have about 4 drinks remaining 3 hours later.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handlebar.
On the right handlebar.
By the left foot peg.
By the right foot peg.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handlebar.
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handlebar. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you are slowing down where other drivers may not expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are slowing down where other drivers may not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicles' brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing where drivers don't expect it, like in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: One that requires your arms to hold you up.
One that lets you easily reach the controls.
One that keeps your arms straight when holding the grips.
One that keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that lets you easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections.
On highways.
On rural roads.
In parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching and crossing intersections.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding in another vehicle's blind spot?

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down and drop back to leave the spot.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should wear tight clothing, not loose clothing that might catch. Passengers should lean with the operator in turns and never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: How can you make night riding safer?

options.text: Night riding is discouraged.
Wear reflective clothing.
Night riding is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Night riding should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When you slow down or stop, what should you do?

options.text: Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.
Take the bike out of gear.
Stay in the same gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that reduces your space cushion and makes others see you.
One that increases your space cushion and makes others see you.
One that increases road hazards and lets others pass you.
One that reduces road hazards and lets you follow closely behind vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your space cushion and makes others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you more space around your motorcycle. This helps others see you, keeps you away from wind blasts and blind spots, avoids road hazards, and gives you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Why should you use both front and rear brakes when slowing or stopping?

options.text: Using one brake wears them unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops builds a habit of using both. This habit is important in emergencies when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Decided by a judge.
Not very harsh.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has mandatory severe penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle will speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you are going too fast when shifting into a lower gear, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Brake only on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Lean with you through turns.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you through turns.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without getting in your way, and hold onto the handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Gradually apply your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because that makes the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not brake, as that can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane will place you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake on a motorcycle is controlled by your right foot.

questions.question: What does it mean when a driver makes eye contact with you?

options.text: They see you.
It will never happen.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
They will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not notice them.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: How should you help drivers merge from an entrance ramp into your lane?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to another lane if you can.
Do not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by moving to another lane if possible.
